source_text: Critics, including a 2016 parliamentary committee, have described the absence of earlier convictions as a "national scandal," pointing to systemic failures in investigation and prosecution amid rising immigration from high-prevalence regions in Africa and the Middle East, where FGM serves non-therapeutic cultural or ritual purposes often justified by unsubstantiated claims of hygiene or maturity despite empirical evidence of long-term physical and psychological harm. [7]
